description: Change of use from Use Class C3 (dwelling house) to Use Class C4 (HMO-house in multiple occupation) involving single storey rear extensions, rear dormer, rear outrigger dormer and front rooflights, with associated amenity, cycle and refuse storage.
decision_conditions: The development hereby permitted must be begun not later than the end of three years from the date of this permission. Reason: To comply with the provisions of S.51 of the Planning & Compulsory Purchase Act 2004.

The development hereby permitted shall be carried out in accordance with the following approved plans:E 00 (Dated 20/03/2026),E 01 (Dated 20/03/2026),E 02 (Dated 20/03/2026),E 03 (Dated 20/03/2026),E 04 (Dated 20/03/2026),E 05 (Dated 20/03/2026),P 00 (Dated 26/03/2026),P 01 (Dated 26/03/2026),P 02 (Dated 26/03/2026),P 03 (Dated 26/03/2026),P 04 (Dated 26/03/2026),P 05 (Dated 26/03/2026),P 06 (Dated 26/03/2026),P 07 (Dated 26/03/2026),P 08 (Dated 26/03/2026),SuDS Pro Forma,Highway Safety Impact Form.Reason: For the avoidance of doubt and in the interests of proper planning.

All new external work shall be carried out in materials that resemble, as closely as possible, in colour and texture as specified in the approved application.Reason: To safeguard the appearance of the premises and the character of the immediate area.

Notwithstanding the details provided within the submitted documents, prior to the first occupation of the HMO hereby permitted, 6 long stay cycle parking spaces to satisfy the permitted number of occupiers on site shall have been fully provided.The dedicated cycle store providing 6 long stay parking spaces shall fulfil the following:-	Have aisles at least 1.5 metres wide to allow for easy manoeuvring.-	Provide a minimum width of at least 1 metre between stands.-	Provide an access door with a minimum width of at least 1.2 metres.-	Be secured with a British Standard mortice lock or access fob to provide greater security.Reason: To ensure that adequate cycle parking facilities are provided to promote sustainable modes of transport.

Notwithstanding the details shown on the submitted drawings, prior to the first occupation of the HMO hereby permitted, waste storage and recycling facilities to satisfy the permitted number of occupiers shall have been provided on site, in accordance with the Enfield's Household Recycling and Waste Planning Guidance for New Developments (February 2024). Such facilities are to be retained thereafter, unless otherwise agreed in writing by the Local Planning Authority.Reason: To ensure that adequate waste and recycling storage facilities are provided to meet the needs of future occupiers, promote sustainable waste management practices, and support borough-wide recycling targets.

The HMO hereby permitted shall not be occupied by more than 6 residents at any one time, unless otherwise agreed in writing by the Local Planning Authority.  Reason: To ensure that the future occupation of the building does not compromise standards of accommodation and does not adversely affect the residential amenities of neighbouring properties.

No independent cooking or laundry facilities shall be installed in any of the respective bedrooms and the ground floor communal kitchen, living and dining room, shall be retained in perpetuity. Reason: To accord with the stipulations of definition as a House of Multiple Occupation and to safeguard the residential character of the surrounding area.
